title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 445
paragraphs: The Corinthians also took part zealously in this expedition against Samos, so that it might be carried out; for an offense had been committed against them as well by the Samians, a generation before this expedition and around the same time as the robbery of the bowl. Periander son of Kypselos had dispatched three hundred sons of the leading men of Corcyra to Alyattes at Sardis to be made eunuchs; and when the Corinthians escorting the boys put in at Samos, the Samians, having learned the story and for what purpose the boys were being conducted to Sardis, first instructed the boys to seize the temple of Artemis, and then refused to permit the Corinthians to drag the suppliants away from the temple. And when the Corinthians cut the boys off from supplies of food, the Samians made a festival, which they celebrate in the same manner to this day. For when night came on, as long as the boys were suppliants, they arranged dances of maidens and youths, and in arranging the dances they made it a rule of the festival that sweet cakes of sesame and honey should be carried, so that the Corcyrean boys might snatch them and so have sustenance. This went on for so long that at last the Corinthians who had charge of the boys departed and went away; and the Samians carried the boys back to Corcyra.
